semantics: Refactor candidates that were investigated, costed and refused, as data rather than prose (.agents/docs/implemented/process/2026-09-20-agent-refactorability-gates.md section 2). Each candidate carries an `id`, the `symbols` that carry its shape, and a `ruling` anchor holding the evidence. src/test-kernel/architecture/refutedCandidatesRatchet.vitest.ts pins every symbol's `signature` — the declaration with its bodies elided as `{…}`, comments stripped, whitespace collapsed — so a symbol that changes shape fails until the baseline entry is updated in the same PR. The gate does not forbid the change; citing the candidate's `id` in the PR body is a convention, not checked. Re-proposing a refused candidate as originally specified is the failure this exists to stop; landing a candidate on NEW evidence is legal, and that PR cites the id, states what changed, and deletes or rewrites the entry.

candidates.candidate: the platform config providers onto an Effect ConfigProvider
candidates.why: Config<T> over the platform port's own get buys nothing: the read stays synchronous and answers for the workspace the caller was handed. Naming each row a second time as Config.Boolean/Config.Int beside the Zod catalog row that owns it is a dual schema system with a ConfigError where Settings.get's validation already stands. Settings stay synchronous by ruling; Effect Config is for process.env reads, a separate lane.

candidates.why: Re-checked on Effect 4.1.0. Semaphore no longer barges (4.0.7), but take, takeScoped and withPermit are Effects that join its queue one evaluation after refuseClaim decides, and the fiber can yield in between (Scheduler.shouldYield at MaxOpsBeforeYield, 2048 by default), so a fiber that claimed later enters first: a one-permit Semaphore per lane did so at 2 of 2101 claim offsets at the default budget and in about half of 150 six-fiber runs at budgets 8 and 13, the Deferred chain never. The chain swaps its tail in the step that runs refuseClaim, which RunRegistry's admission relies on. An RcMap of semaphores would own the lane map each caller passes (RunRegistry keeps its lanes on its run entries, two callers key a WeakMap), needs a Scope to build, and answers get as an Effect, so refuseClaim could not read the occupant in the claim step. The lane maps prune themselves, so making them services is a pure net-add.

candidates.candidate: ModelRetryGate onto the effect/persistence CircuitBreaker, with Effect.retry on its rejections behind the unchanged withRoutes
candidates.why: The breaker cannot keep the gate's backoff rule. Its opening count survives a close and resets only by time, once the circuit has stayed closed as long as it was last open (node_modules/effect/src/persistence/CircuitBreaker.ts:15-16, :1143-1146, :1195, effect 4.1.0); a success while closed clears only the trip streak (:1204), and the next opening counts from the count the failing call started under (:480). The gate ends its streak on the first clean round-trip of a healthy route and never on a probe success (packages/harness/src/agent/runtime/ModelRetryGate.ts:165-168, :326-337, from #9078), so a released herd that fails at once grows the backoff while a route failing between successes stays at the base. Measured with one clean success between each recovery and the next failure: the gate cooled 1000 ms seven times; the breaker (jittered exponential from 1 s, capped at 5 min, midpoint jitter) opened for 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000 and 64000 ms. Every 5xx, 408 and 429 not scoped to the model cools the whole wire route (packages/llm/src/errors.ts:155-156), so an intermittently overloaded provider would stall every run on that credential toward the 5-minute cap; a constant openDuration brings back the herd re-failing at the base backoff that #9078 fixed. The breaker also never waits (CircuitBreaker.ts:18-21, :1149-1162) and withRoutes cannot add an error, so it would poll for as long as the probe runs, a whole billed turn (packages/harness/src/agent/runtime/run/invocation.ts:203-219), where the gate queues callers, hands the probe to the oldest (ModelRetryGate.ts:424) and releases the rest the moment it succeeds (:338-357). classify sees only the exit, not whether the call is the probe (CircuitBreaker.ts:570-585); openDuration is fixed per breaker (:452-457) where baseBackoffMs is per call; the module is @stability experimental (:121).
